blocks.title: Smartphones are now an integral part of daily life. Many people use their phones before bed — for social media, messaging, gaming, or watching videos. However, it is not fully understood how different types of phone interactions influence sleep.

block2.title: About the Sleep Hygiene Study
block2.content:
The Study of Sleep Hygiene and Health is a citizen science research project investigating how smartphone use — particularly before bedtime — influences sleep quality, duration, and overall sleep hygiene.
By combining wearable device data, smartphone usage information, and short daily questionnaires, we aim to better understand the relationship between digital behaviour and sleep in real-world settings.
Partners: King's College London, South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust.

block1.title: Our Aims
block1.subtitle: Our goal is to generate evidence that can inform healthier digital habits and improve sleep hygiene recommendations.

block2.content:
Investigate whether increased screen time before sleep is associated with:


Delayed sleep onset
Shorter sleep duration
Reduced sleep efficiency

Examine whether different app categories (e.g., social media, gaming, productivity) have different effects on sleep

Compare sleep patterns across different age groups

Explore long-term sleep behaviour over several months

block1.title: Who Can Take Part
block1.subtitle:
No diagnosed medical condition is required — this is a general population study.
You can withdraw from the study at any time.

block2.content:
Are 13 years or older

Regularly use a smartphone & Own a wearable device

Install two secure research apps on your smartphone

Wear your device regularly, including overnight

blocks.title: Benefits
blocks.content: Although there is no direct financial reward. However:

block1.title: Contributing to research on digital wellbeing and sleep health

block2.title: Receive a summary of your own sleep data at the end of the study

block3.title: Help improve public health recommendations around screen time and sleep

block1.title: Phone Data is Collected
block1.content: Track your app usage and screen habits

block2.title: Sleep Data is Collected
block2.content: Monitor your sleep, heart rate and movement patterns through your wearable device

block3.title: Answer Questionnaires
block3.content: Recieve short daily questionnaires about your sleep and mood

block4.title: Analayse Patterns Overtime
block4.content: Researchers will analyse the sleep data over several months to identify patterns and insights

block1.title: Wear Your Wearable Device
block1.content: We will ask you to wear your fitness tracker or smart device as much as possible during the study (for at least 3 months, optionally up to 12 months). From this, we will measure Sleep duration, Sleep stages (where available), Sleep onset and offset, Heart rate, Physical activity

block2.subtitle: Use The RADAR-base Apps
block2.content: RADAR Passive App and RADAR Active App

block3.subtitle: Take The Cognitive Tests
block3.content: You will be invited to complete short online cognitive tasks using the Cognitron platform to explore how sleep and phone use relate to attention and thinking performance.

items.title: How long does the study last?
items.content: The minimum participation we need is 3 months. But there is an option for a possible extension up to 12 months.

items.title: What will happen to the data?
items.content:
Your data will be used to:
Analysed to understand patterns of smartphone use and sleep.
Used to publish scientific findings (you will never be identifiable).
Potentially shared in de-identified form with approved researchers worldwide (if you consent).
You may choose whether or not your anonymised data can be shared for future research.

items.title: How is my data protected?
items.content:
Your privacy is extremely important to us.
Your data is processed in accordance with the UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 where all data are de-identified using a unique study ID.
Your name and contact details are stored separately and securely.
We do not access the content of messages or calls Relative location data are offset to prevent identification.
King’s College London is the study sponsor and data controller.

items.title: What wearable can I use?
items.content: The devices that are compatible are Fitbit, Oura Ring, Garmin, Apple Watch, Polar, Empatica E4.

items.title: Are there any risks?
items.content:
Risks are minimal.
The study requires a small amount of time for questionnaires.
There is a very small cybersecurity risk similar to everyday smartphone use.
If you feel uncomfortable with our data collection — you may withdraw at any time with/without giving a reason. You may request deletion of identifiable data within the first 30 days.
